title: SNOMED: all 464,018 UUID-shaped codes are INVALID (not the UK drug extension) — so a numeric-only default has ZERO false negatives on valid concepts
content:
DISCOVERED 2026-07-27 while reviewing Odie's SNOMED row, which added a UUID alternation and described
the UUIDs as 'retired UK Drug extension'. Both halves of that were off.

## NOT the UK drug extension
UUID-shaped SNOMED codes by concept_class:
    Physical Object      194,791       Qualifier Value    8,735
    Pharma/Biol Product  192,709       Substance          2,786
    Context-dependent     64,755       Model Comp           183
Physical Object is the LARGEST bucket; Context-dependent, Qualifier Value and Model Comp are not drugs
at all. So the UUID form is not an extension-specific encoding.

## What it actually is: THE RETIRED PORTION OF SNOMED, ENTIRELY
    UUID-shaped (464,018):  invalid_reason='U' 367,198  ·  'D' 96,820  ·  **VALID: 0**
    numeric IDs (629,129):  349,211 valid+standard, plus U/D/non-standard
Not one UUID-shaped code is a valid concept. Measured:
    ^[0-9]+$  vs ALL SNOMED concept_codes    ->  464,018 false negatives
    ^[0-9]+$  vs VALID SNOMED concept_codes  ->  **0 false negatives**

## DECIDED (Ryan, 2026-07-27)
Default `SNOMED` -> `^[0-9]+$`. Ryan: 'I'd favor a regexp for non-uk drug extension as our default
snomed format, then use the standard regexp for uuid for snomed.plusukdrugext or something.'
The instinct was right and the justification is stronger than the framing: it is not that the drug
extension is a special case, it is that **every UUID code is retired**, so a numeric-only default
rejects nothing valid.
NAMING: the variant should be named for what it IS — retired/withdrawn concepts — NOT for the UK drug
extension, which is not what distinguishes them. Something like SNOMED.WITHRETIRED.
Cost avoided: Odie's alternation made the regex accept ANY UUID as a SNOMED code, in exchange for
covering 464k concepts of which none is valid.

## Fits the claims principle
SNOMED barely appears in US claims at all — it is in this repo because litmine extracts it from
PAPERS. So the claims-default rule does not really bite here; what does is 'valid vs retired', and
numeric-only happens to be exactly the valid set. Convenient, and worth noting it is a coincidence of
SNOMED's encoding history rather than a general pattern.

title: Add a SECOND table: the vocab-label id-normalization REGISTRY (verbatim label seen in the wild -> OHDSI vocabulary_id, or BLANK = not supported in OHDSI)
content:
Decided by Ryan across litmine's lit-et6.1 (2026-07-23 refinement) and refined 2026-07-24. Filed HERE
2026-07-25 during the codesets seed-reconciliation pass — the decision was fully specified but lived
only in litmine's seed tree, and this repo had no seeds at all.

## The decision
vocabulary_formats gains a SECOND table alongside the format regexes: an **ID-normalization map**
from a vocabulary label 'hit in the wild' -> a known-good OHDSI `vocabulary_id`.
Examples: 'ICD-10-CM' -> ICD10CM; WHO 'ICD-10' -> ICD10; 'CPT' / 'CPT-4' -> CPT4.

## It is a REGISTRY, not just a mapping (Ryan, 2026-07-24)
Every vocabulary label encountered in the literature is recorded **verbatim**, and each row resolves
to EITHER a known-good OHDSI vocabulary_id OR a **BLANK** id meaning 'this vocabulary is not
supported in OHDSI (as of now)'. Ryan's words: 'if the vocab doesn't exist, we record it as it
appears in the literature into that mapping file and either derive a mapping or leave the mapping
with no OHDSI ID to indicate that the vocab isn't supported in OHDSI.'

Consequences:
- The table is the COMPLETE registry of labels seen + their OHDSI status — one source of truth.
  A new unseen label is appended verbatim, then mapped or left blank.
- **A blank id IS the non-OMOP gate.** litmine's 'extract but don't produce' set (lit-et6.3) is
  exactly the blank rows; no separate list is needed.
- Provenance preserved (verbatim label is the key) and omission is VISIBLE — a blank loudly marks
  'not in OHDSI' rather than a code set silently vanishing.
- Blank means 'unsupported AS OF NOW' — revisitable when OHDSI or an OI supplemental vocab adds it.
- A genuinely MISLABELED code (a paper calls ICD10CM 'ICD-10') is caught downstream by the
  format/existence check. The map is best-effort; the concept DB is the backstop.

## Why it belongs here and not in code
Separation of concerns, decided with Ryan: **vocabulary_formats stays DATA-ONLY and polyglot** — the
Ruby catalog and both Python producers read the same files. Adding Python would break its
language-neutral value. The CODE that consumes it lives in **codesistant** (repo created 2026-07-23,
beads cst-*), which reads BOTH tables (format regexes + id-normalization).

## Downstream consumers
- codesistant reads it for producer-side vocab-name alignment.
- code_collector's `vocab_mappings.csv` (21 rows, name -> OHDSI id) eventually MIGRATES here.
- Its non-blank ids feed the extraction-time enum litmine is considering (lit-et6.4) — deriving the
  enum from this column keeps the enum and the format regexes from drifting apart.

## Authoring
Hand the entries to a domain agent — Odie (OHDSI/OMOP) or Vincent (vocab) or the vocabulary habitat —
to author and validate, rather than guessing ids.


BEAD FILED 2026-07-25: **vocabulary_formats-e5s**.



## CPT4_HCPCS IS A FIRST-CLASS MAPPING TARGET (Ryan, 2026-07-25) — and the PREFERRED one for procedures

Ryan, raising this specifically: 'we'll especially need to do that with HCPCS/CPT as those are divided
in OHDSI and we unioned them.' The union exists and is verified in the substrate:

    vocabulary_id **CPT4_HCPCS** — 30,357 concepts; CPT4 18,069 + HCPCS 12,822 = 30,891, 534 deduped.
    vocabulary_version is NULL -> an OI SUPPLEMENTAL vocabulary, not stock Athena.
    Decided in code_set_catalog csc-171 (2026-06-02); catalog-side wiring is bead csc-meqj.

### Why this changes the registry's spec as written above
This seed says each row maps to 'a known-good OHDSI vocabulary_id'. Taken literally that excludes
CPT4_HCPCS (it is an OI supplemental, not stock OHDSI) and pushes the naive mappings
'CPT' -> CPT4 and 'HCPCS' -> HCPCS — **which re-creates precisely the split csc-171 exists to heal.**

So: the target column is 'a vocabulary_id in OUR substrate', which INCLUDES OI supplementals.
CPT4_HCPCS is a legal, and for procedure labels the PREFERRED, target — matching csc-171's
'hybrid is the recommended default; originals stay selectable'.

### The concrete rows this affects (real labels from litmine's 20-paper pilot)
    'CPT'          (23 code sets)  -> CPT4_HCPCS   (not CPT4)
    'CPT-4'         (6)            -> CPT4_HCPCS
    'HCPCS'         (4)            -> CPT4_HCPCS   (not HCPCS)
    'CPT/HCPCS'     (1)            -> CPT4_HCPCS   <- has NO other home
    'mixed procedure codes (CPT, CPT Category III/PLA, HCPCS Level II, ICD-10-PCS); labeled only
     "Procedures" by the authors' (1)            -> needs a call: CPT4_HCPCS loses the ICD-10-PCS
     part, so this may be a genuine multi-vocabulary set requiring a producer-side SPLIT (rule 4)
     rather than a single mapping. Flag rather than guess.

Without this, the last two map to BLANK and are silently dropped by lit-et6.3's
extract-but-don't-produce gate — a perfectly good procedure code set lost, which is exactly the
omission failure habitat rule 7 names as the primary risk.

### Note on 'preferred'
Mapping 'CPT' -> CPT4_HCPCS is a WIDENING: the label said CPT, the target covers CPT+HCPCS. That is
correct for BINDING (a CPT code resolves in the hybrid) but the verbatim label stays 'CPT', so no
provenance is lost. If a consumer ever needs the narrow reading, it has the verbatim key. Worth
stating explicitly in the table's notes column so a future reader does not 'fix' it back.



## THE REGISTRY IS NOW FED BY THE HARVEST (Ryan, 2026-08-04)

Ruling on the upstream-vs-downstream fork that this table was always the downstream half of:
**"extract vocabulary as it is written in the paper and we will use that information to form a
comprehensive mapping in vocabulary_formats."** Recorded in full on litmine's lit-et6.4.

**What it settles for this table.** There will be no closed vocabulary enum at extraction time. The
verbatim label is captured exactly as the paper spelled it, and THIS registry is the only place
normalization happens. That makes the table load-bearing rather than convenient: if a label has no
row, the code set it belongs to is dropped by the extract-but-don't-produce gate (lit-et6.3), so a
missing row is a silent data loss of exactly the kind habitat rule 7 names as the primary failure.

**What it changes about how the table GROWS.** The rows above came from a 20-paper pilot — 22
free-text labels for ~14 real vocabularies. The harvest is now planned against 11K+ papers
(code_collector clc-pdr, corrected 2026-08-04), so the observed-label set will be much larger and
will keep arriving. Two consequences:

1. **The registry is never complete before a harvest, and that is fine.** Design for continuous
   extension, not a one-time authoring pass. What is NOT fine is an unmapped label failing quietly —
   every miss must be surfaced and counted at render time so a human can decide whether it needs a
   row, a `multi_vocabulary` split, or a genuine `unsupported` blank.
2. **The harvest becomes this repo's best source of real-world labels.** Every way the literature
   actually spells a vocabulary, at volume. That is more comprehensive than anything authored from
   the OHDSI vocabulary list alone, and it serves every consumer of this table, not just the
   literature pipeline.

**Unchanged:** the target column is "a vocabulary_id in OUR substrate," including OI supplementals
(CPT4_HCPCS stays the preferred target for procedure labels, per csc-171), and mapping 'CPT' ->
CPT4_HCPCS remains a deliberate WIDENING that loses no provenance because the verbatim label is the
key. Authoring/validating new rows still goes to a domain agent (Odie or Vincent) rather than being
guessed by the producer.

title: Extend the format regexes beyond claims vocabs to cover litmine's non-claims vocabularies (WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD10PCS, ATC, DRG, ICD-O-3)
content:
Decided by Ryan in litmine's lit-et6.1 (2026-07-23). Filed HERE 2026-07-25 during the codesets
seed-reconciliation pass — the work was decided but lived only in litmine's seed tree.

## The gap
The current table is 13 rows covering CLAIMS vocabularies only: ICD9CM (+.DOTLESS), ICD10CM
(+.DOTLESS), HCPCS (± modifiers), CPT4 (± modifiers), NDC (+.ALPHANUM). litmine extracts code sets in
whatever vocabulary a paper used, so it needs rows for **WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD10PCS, ATC,
DRG, ICD-O-3** and whatever else the corpus turns up.

Ryan: 'tens of rows at most', cheap — and fine to grow an asset several repos depend on.

## Keep them PERMISSIVE — this is the load-bearing constraint
Per this repo's own README the regexes are deliberately 'skewed toward valid': accept anything that
COULD be a valid code, tolerate false positives, **NEVER reject a real code**. False negatives are
unacceptable (hence the loose ICD10CM \w{3}.\w{0,4} so future U-codes still pass).

Strict/existence validation is explicitly OUT of scope — it belongs to the concept DB, which is where
the set of all known-good codes actually lives. A regex validates FORMAT ('does this look like a code
of vocab X?'); it cannot validate EXISTENCE. You can't pattern your way to 'E11.9 is real but E11.99
is not', and a tight regex goes stale as codes change yearly.

**The two layers together are more useful than either alone** — they classify failures on different
axes: passes-format-but-misses-DB = 'well-formed but not a real code' (typo / retired / non-US
variant); fails-format = malformed. That is exactly litmine's validate.py taxonomy
(valid_fy2025 / valid_earlier_fy / format_valid_not_found / invalid), already in production.

## Two field-tested constraints to inherit rather than rediscover
From Mark's litmine handoff, both hit by his recall scanner:
1. **The dotted-code trap.** An undotted-only regex truncates `M05.79` to the category `M05`,
   collapsing a 338-code list into ~12 hits and scoring a code-rich paper as empty. Any scan must
   handle BOTH forms — direct field confirmation of why the `.DOTLESS` variants exist, and a warning
   that a consumer reading only one variant silently UNDER-COUNTS rather than erroring.
2. **A >=4-character floor** stops bare 3-char categories in ordinary disease prose (`F10`, `I21`)
   from matching. This is a SCANNING threshold, not a validation one — a real 3-char code like
   `I10` is legitimately valid — so **the floor belongs in the CALLER, not in the format regex.**
   Worth stating explicitly as the regexes gain new consumers: it is exactly the kind of rule that
   gets pushed down into the shared layer by mistake.

## Mechanics
Edit the TSV; `make all` regenerates the parquet. Keyed by OHDSI `vocabulary_id`, which is also the
join key to the id-normalization registry (vfm-31w).

## Authoring
Hand the new regexes to a domain agent — Odie (OHDSI/OMOP) or Vincent (vocab) or the vocabulary
habitat — to author and validate.

## NB — repo is dirty
As of 2026-07-25 this repo has uncommitted changes to README.md and vocabulary_formats.tsv plus
untracked CLAUDE.md / Makefile / vocabulary_formats.parquet, all with mtimes from 2024-2026-02
(stale, not live work). Reconcile those before adding rows.


BEAD FILED 2026-07-25: **vocabulary_formats-3h8**.


## THE WORKING TREE ALREADY VIOLATES THIS (found 2026-07-25) — see bead vocabulary_formats-1n1
The 'NB — repo is dirty' note above understated it. The stale uncommitted changes are not inert:
they TIGHTEN three regexes, and the ICD10CM one is a correctness regression.
    committed:   ^\w{3}.?\w{0,4}$   (dot optional)
    uncommitted: ^\w{3}\.\w{0,4}$    (dot required)
Tested: I10, E11, F10, N18 all go PASS -> FAIL. Three-character ICD-10-CM codes are real, and in the
OHDSI concept table they live in the DOTTED vocabulary with no dot (verified against the June-2026
Athena build). So the 'permissive, never reject a real code' rule this seed records as a hard
constraint is already broken in the working tree — by an edit nobody documented, in a repo that had
no seeds or beads to record intent, which is exactly the gap this seed and vfm-31w were filed to close.
Resolve vocabulary_formats-1n1 BEFORE adding non-claims rows on top of an unreviewed base.

title: NDC: the committed regex rejected 338,328 real codes (26% of the vocabulary); default becomes 11-digit (claims), NDC.COMPLETE carries 9+11
content:
DISCOVERED by Odie 2026-07-27 while extending the regexes, verified independently the same day.

## The bug
    NDC  ^\d{11}$  vs 1,302,950 real concept_codes  ->  **338,328 false negatives (26%)**
Of those, 337,085 are 9-digit NDCs and 1,218 are 9-digit Devices. This is the largest false-negative
count in the repo by a wide margin — 170x the ICD10CM regression fixed earlier the same day (1,953).
It had been shipping since the repo's first commit.

## WHY it happened — and this is the useful part
The 9-digit form is not an error or a legacy artifact. OHDSI classes them explicitly:
    len=11  class '11-digit NDC'   953,259    <- labeler-product-PACKAGE: the billing form
    len= 9  class '9-digit NDC'    337,085    <- FDA labeler+product, no package segment
    len=11  class 'Device'          11,388
    len= 9  class 'Device'           1,218
So the regex was correct for CLAIMS and wrong for the VOCABULARY, and nobody had written down which
of those the row was for. The bug is a symptom of the missing purpose statement — see the
two-consumer principle seed.

## DECIDED (Ryan, 2026-07-27)
    NDC           ^\d{11}$              <- claims default (the billing form)
    NDC.COMPLETE  ^(\d{9}|\d{11})$      <- the full vocabulary
Ryan: 'perhaps we should also have ndc.complete as 9 and 11 and default ndc to 11 only — my primary
goal for vocabulary_formats is to find codes we'd expect to see in claims data.'
This supersedes Odie's fix, which widened the DEFAULT to `^(\d{9}|\d{11})$`. His widening was right
about the facts and wrong about which row should carry them: it made the default mean 'everything in
the vocabulary', which is the drift the principle seed forbids.

## LETTERS IN NDC — asked and answered (Ryan)
'Is a letter ever a valid part of an NDC code?' **Yes, but barely: 39 of 1,302,950 (0.003%).**
    len=11  '11-digit NDC'  valid      24
    len= 9  '9-digit NDC'   valid      14
    len=11  '11-digit NDC'  invalid=D   1
38 are VALID concepts and OHDSI classes them as ordinary 9-/11-digit NDCs despite the letter. They are
radiopharmaceutical kits ('KIT FOR THE PREPARATION OF TECHNETIUM TC 99M...'), and they do NOT share a
single labeler prefix. So NDC.ALPHANUM earns its keep as a genuine long tail — but 39 codes is not a
reason to loosen any default.

## METHODOLOGY TRAP worth recording
A first pass answering the letters question used DuckDB's `~` operator and reported ZERO. **DuckDB's
`~` is NOT a regex-match operator** — `SELECT '000199092B0' ~ '[A-Za-z]'` returns FALSE while
`regexp_matches('000199092B0','[A-Za-z]')` returns TRUE. Any validation in this repo must use
regexp_matches or scan in Python; `~` will silently report false negatives as clean.

title: multi_vocabulary rows leave the producer re-parsing PROSE — should the registry carry component vocabulary_ids?
content:
A `multi_vocabulary` row records that a label names more than one vocabulary, leaves `vocabulary_id`
blank, and README says the remedy is "a producer-side split into per-vocabulary code sets, not a
single mapping." The POLICY is settled (habitat rule 4: one vocabulary per code set). The DATA to
execute it is not here.

## The problem, in one row

    label          mixed procedure codes (CPT, CPT Category III/PLA, HCPCS Level II, ICD-10-PCS);
                   labeled only "Procedures" by the authors
    vocabulary_id  (blank)
    status         multi_vocabulary
    notes          FLAGGED, do not map. CPT4_HCPCS would silently drop the ICD-10-PCS members.

Everything a producer needs to perform the split is present — and present only as PROSE, inside a
free-text label and a free-text note. To act on it, a producer must re-read English and infer
{CPT4_HCPCS, ICD10PCS}. That is a model decision standing in for a lookup, which is exactly what
Mark's invariant #4 ("routing decisions that can be computed are computed") says not to build, and
exactly the failure mode that motivated killing the extraction-time vocabulary enum (lit-et6.4): a
model re-deriving something a table could state.

The second such row makes it sharper, because its components are NOT recoverable from prose alone:

    ICD-9-CM / ICD-10-CM (mixed; printed as one unlabeled list)

Here the split is not even a partition by label — it needs per-CODE adjudication, since the paper
printed one undifferentiated list. Two multi_vocabulary rows, two different kinds of split.

## The question

Should a `multi_vocabulary` row carry its COMPONENT vocabulary_ids as data — a delimited list in a
new column, or the row expanded into several — so the producer's split is a lookup?

Points to weigh:

- **For:** it is the same argument that won lit-et6.4. Whoever adjudicated the row already knew the
  components; discarding that into prose forces every downstream consumer to re-derive it.
- **For:** it makes the split auditable. A component list can be checked; an inference cannot.
- **Against:** the two rows split by different MECHANISMS. Row 1 partitions by code format
  (a CPT code and an ICD-10-PCS code are distinguishable by shape, so the format regexps can route
  them). Row 2 needs code-by-code adjudication against the concept table, because ICD-9-CM and
  ICD-10-CM overlap in shape. A single "components" column would imply these are the same operation
  when they are not — and might invite a producer to attempt row 2 mechanically and get it wrong.
- **Against (scope):** this repo is data-only and deliberately dumb. A components column edges toward
  encoding an algorithm in the table.
- **Middle option:** carry the components AND a `split_by` discriminator (`format` vs `lookup`), so
  the data says both what the parts are and whether they are mechanically separable.

## Why it matters more now than at the pilot

Two multi_vocabulary rows out of 22 came from 20 papers. Verbatim extraction across 11K+ papers
(Ryan, 2026-08-04) will produce these at volume, and every unresolved one is a real code set dropped
— the omission failure habitat rule 7 names. At two rows a human can read the prose. At two hundred
they cannot.

## Not to be resolved here alone

The consuming side is the producer's renderer (code_collector after the litmine merge). Whatever this
seed concludes, the split itself is filed there, and habitat routing says new mappings go to a domain
agent (Odie or Vincent) to author and validate rather than being guessed producer-side.

Related: vfm-31w (the registry's design), and beads vocabulary_formats-wyf / -7dl (the two contract
items filed 2026-08-04).

title: Ryan's three questions on Odie's regexes: letters in NDC (yes, 39), SNOMED UUIDs (NOT UK-drug — ALL invalid, so numeric-only has 0 FN on valid codes), and the claims/billable purpose
content:
Three questions from Ryan, 2026-07-27, reviewing Odie's regex work. All answered against the
June-2026 Athena build. NOTE a methodology trap hit while answering: **DuckDB's `~` is NOT a regex
match operator** — `SELECT '000199092B0' ~ '[A-Za-z]'` returns FALSE while
`regexp_matches('000199092B0','[A-Za-z]')` returns TRUE. A first pass using `~` reported "0 NDC codes
contain a letter", which was a silent false negative. Use regexp_matches, or scan in Python.

=== Q1: "is a letter ever a valid part of an NDC code?" — YES, but barely ===
**39 of 1,302,950 (0.003%).** Breakdown:
    len=11  class '11-digit NDC'  valid       24
    len=9   class '9-digit NDC'   valid       14
    len=11  class '11-digit NDC'  invalid=D    1
So 38 are VALID concepts, and OHDSI classes them as ordinary 9-/11-digit NDCs despite the letter.
They are radiopharmaceutical kits ("KIT FOR THE PREPARATION OF TECHNETIUM TC 99M..."). They do NOT
all share one labeler prefix.
CONSEQUENCE: NDC.ALPHANUM earns its place, but it covers 39 codes — it is a genuine long tail, not a
significant share. Worth keeping as a variant; not worth loosening the default for.

=== Q2: "are all UUIDs in SNOMED the UK drug extension?" — NO. And the real answer is stronger ===
Odie characterised the 464,018 UUID-shaped SNOMED codes as "retired UK Drug extension". Wrong on the
first half, and it undersells the second.
NOT UK-drug-specific — by concept_class:
    Physical Object      194,791      Qualifier Value    8,735
    Pharma/Biol Product  192,709      Substance          2,786
    Context-dependent     64,755      Model Comp           183
Physical Object is the LARGEST bucket, and Context-dependent / Qualifier Value / Model Comp are not
drugs at all.

**But every single one is INVALID:**
    UUID-shaped (464,018):  invalid_reason='U' 367,198   invalid_reason='D' 96,820   VALID: 0
    numeric IDs (629,129):  VALID+standard 349,211, plus U/D/non-standard
So the UUIDs are not a UK extension — they are **the retired portion of SNOMED, in its entirety**.
Measured directly:
    ^[0-9]+$  vs ALL SNOMED concept_codes      -> 464,018 false negatives
    ^[0-9]+$  vs VALID SNOMED concept_codes    -> **0 false negatives**

**RYAN'S PROPOSAL IS CORRECT AND BETTER-FOUNDED THAN HE PUT IT.** A numeric-only default has ZERO
false negatives against every valid SNOMED concept. Odie's UUID alternation was protecting 464k codes
of which none is valid — and the cost was real: it made the regex accept any UUID as a SNOMED code.
RECOMMEND: default `SNOMED` -> `^[0-9]+$`; keep the UUID form as a variant if a consumer ever needs
retired concepts (name it for what it is — retired/withdrawn — rather than for the UK extension,
which is not what it is).

=== Q3: "primary goal is codes we'd expect in claims data, mostly billable" — YES, and it is the ===
=== repo's NATIVE purpose, not a new one. But it now has a second consumer.                     ===
The framing is already visible in the existing rows: the `.DOTLESS` variants exist because "Medicare
claims data often reports these without the dot". That is a claims-shaped concern. So the claims
target is original, not a reframe.

NDC supports the proposal cleanly:
    len=11  class '11-digit NDC'   953,259     <- the billing form (labeler-product-package)
    len= 9  class '9-digit NDC'    337,085     <- FDA labeler+product, no package segment
    len=11  class 'Device'          11,388
    len= 9  class 'Device'           1,218
OHDSI's own class names draw exactly the distinction Ryan is drawing. So:
    NDC           -> ^\d{11}$              (claims default)
    NDC.COMPLETE  -> ^(\d{9}|\d{11})$      (everything in the vocabulary)
This also fits the repo's established naming: the DEFAULT is the common/expected case and VARIANTS
name the deviation (.DOTLESS, .WITHMODIFIERS, .ALPHANUM). `.COMPLETE` reads correctly as "the whole
vocabulary, not just what you'd see on a claim".

**THE TENSION WORTH NAMING — the repo now serves two consumers with different needs:**
1. CLAIMS canonicalization (the original): billable, claims-observable codes. Ryan's framing.
2. LITERATURE validation (new, via litmine): ANY real code a paper printed, which includes
   non-claims vocabularies. SNOMED barely appears in US claims at all — it is in this repo because
   litmine extracts it from papers, not because it shows up in a claim.
Those pull in opposite directions, and the variant pattern is exactly how to serve both without
choosing: default = claims-shaped, `.COMPLETE`/`.ALPHANUM`/retired-variant = the full vocabulary.
What must NOT happen is the default quietly drifting toward "everything real", which is how the NDC
row ended up rejecting 26% of its own vocabulary while nobody noticed the purpose had blurred.

RECOMMEND stating the two-consumer split explicitly in README.md, because "never reject a real code"
and "codes you'd expect in claims" are different contracts and the repo currently claims only the
first while Ryan intends primarily the second.


## AGREED AND APPLIED (Ryan, 2026-07-27): 'I agree with your conclusions and proposed ideas'
All three answers are now DECISIONS, split into their own seeds:
  vfm-k2n  the claims-default PRINCIPLE (trellis candidate)
  vfm-8l5  NDC — the 338,328-FN bug, default 11-digit, NDC.COMPLETE for 9+11, letters answered
  vfm-27p  SNOMED — UUIDs are entirely retired, numeric-only default, SNOMED.WITHRETIRED variant
Applied to the working tree and validated through the regenerated parquet:
    NDC                vs 11-digit codes (its target)      964,647   FN=25  (all alphanumeric)
    NDC.COMPLETE       vs all NDC concept_codes          1,302,950   FN=39  (all alphanumeric)
    SNOMED             vs VALID SNOMED only                412,033   FN= 0
    SNOMED.WITHRETIRED vs all SNOMED concept_codes       1,093,147   FN= 0
The alphanumeric residuals are NDC.ALPHANUM's job by design, not misses.
README gained the claims-target contract and the scoped false-negative rule.

title: PRINCIPLE: the default regex targets CLAIMS-OBSERVABLE codes; variants carry the full vocabulary — the repo has two consumers and the default must not drift toward 'everything real'
content:
DECIDED (Ryan, 2026-07-27): 'my primary goal for vocabulary_formats is to find codes we'd expect to
see in claims data so, mostly billable.'

## The principle
For each vocabulary, the DEFAULT row targets what you would expect to see in CLAIMS DATA. Anything
broader — the full vocabulary, retired concepts, alternate encodings — goes in a NAMED VARIANT.

This is not a new direction. It is already visible in the oldest rows: the `.DOTLESS` variants exist
because 'Medicare claims data often reports these without the dot'. The claims target is native to
the repo; it had simply never been written down, and the default drifted without anyone noticing.

## Why it needs stating — the repo now has TWO consumers pulling opposite ways
1. **Claims canonicalization** (original): billable, claims-observable codes. Producers canonicalize
   codes harvested from claims-shaped sources before the catalog's exact join.
2. **Literature validation** (new, via litmine): ANY real code a paper printed, including
   non-claims vocabularies. SNOMED is in this repo because litmine extracts it from PAPERS, not
   because it appears on a US claim.
The variant pattern serves both without choosing. The failure mode is the DEFAULT quietly widening to
mean 'everything real' — which is exactly how the NDC row came to reject 26% of its own vocabulary
while nobody noticed the purpose had blurred (see the NDC sibling seed).

## How this interacts with 'never reject a real code'
It does NOT overturn it; it scopes it. Within a row's stated target, false negatives remain
unacceptable — the ICD10CM regression (1,953 real 3-char codes rejected) and the NDC one (338,328)
are still bugs, because both rejected codes squarely inside the row's own target.
What changes: the TARGET is now explicit per row, so 'is this a false negative?' has an answerable
scope. A 9-digit NDC failing the claims-default `NDC` row is CORRECT; failing `NDC.COMPLETE` is a bug.

## Consequence for README.md
The README currently claims only 'never reject a real code'. That is the second consumer's contract.
State both: the default is claims-shaped, variants carry the rest, and false negatives are judged
against the row's declared target. Without that, the next agent widening a default is doing the
reasonable thing under the documented contract.

## TRELLIS CANDIDATE
This is a durable, always-on rule for the repo — it governs every future row. Worth promoting into
vocabulary_formats' CLAUDE.md once the wording settles.
